definitions.explanation: An individual panel in a manga or a single frame in a film or animation.
A unit of scheduled time, typically referring to a university lecture period or a scheduled slot in a timetable.

examples.japanese: この{漫画|まんが}は1ページに4コマある。
examples.english: This manga has four panels per page.

examples.japanese: 4コマ{漫画|まんが}は{短|みじか}くて{読|よ}みやすい。
examples.english: Four-panel manga are short and easy to read.

examples.japanese: {映画|えいが}のコマを{一|ひと}つずつ{確認|かくにん}した。
examples.english: I checked each frame of the film one by one.

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}は3コマ{授業|じゅぎょう}がある。
examples.english: I have three class periods today.

examples.japanese: 1{限目|げんめ}のコマは{朝|あさ}{早|はや}くて{大変|たいへん}だ。
examples.english: The first-period slot is tough because it's so early in the morning.

examples.japanese: {来学期|らいがっき}は{空|あ}きコマを{減|へ}らしたい。
examples.english: Next semester, I want to reduce my free periods.

notes:
USAGE:
コマ is written in katakana for both senses. The manga/film sense is by far the most common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- 4コマ{漫画|まんが} (four-panel manga — a popular format)
- コマ{割|わ}り (panel layout in manga)
- コマ{送|おく}り (frame-by-frame playback)
- {空|あ}きコマ (free period, gap in schedule)

HOMOPHONE NOTE:
Not to be confused with {駒|こま} (chess/shogi piece; horse) or {独楽|こま} (spinning top), which are different words with different kanji.
